theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Energy (+1.09%) and Utilities (+0.57%) led the market today, while Consumer Discretionary (-1.72%) and Technology (-1.53%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -1.42% versus +0.32% for defensives and -0.57% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 -0.71%, Dow -0.79%, Nasdaq -1.03% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -1.23%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX rose 9.52% to 16.34, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 2.51% to $4,374.30, crude oil was little changed at $90.80, and bitcoin slipped 1.64% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
